Do these steps in order when you first join. After that, pick the guide for whatever you want to do. Updated 22 Oct 2026

If you want to… Start here Pick a class and learn its skills Classes Craft weapons, armour, tools or consumables Advanced Crafting Farm crops, fish or collect materials Farming Cook food or brew drinks Cooking Learn magic Magic Trade with other players Denar Economy Look up a command Command Index

Link your Discord account. You cannot play in Survival until you do. Join the TFMC Discord server, type /linkdiscord in game to get a code, then run /linkdiscord <code> in the Discord server. The game confirms the link within a second or so. More on linking Create a character. On the character selection screen you see when you join, choose New character, then Create character. You choose a name, class, race, traits and attributes, and write a short description, so set aside some time. Until you pick a character, you cannot chat or use any command except /linkdiscord and /rpcharacter menu. Character guide Claim your starter kit. Type /rpcharacter kit starter for a knife, 32 gold coins, 32 dry rations, a book, a bundle and a bed. Learn how chat works. By default, anything you type without a command is spoken by your character and heard within 15 blocks. Use /ooc to talk out of character to the whole server. Chat channels Find a crafting station. Most custom items are made at stations: ordinary-looking blocks that open a custom menu when you right-click them, or sneak and right-click for a few of them. Every recipe in this guide names the station that makes it, and the stations guide shows how to open each one. Crafting Stations
Guns are put together from parts at the Gunsmithing Station. Anyone can build one, but only a Musketeer can fire it. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Ammunition is made at the Alchemy Station from one ingot, with no perk needed. Add one Gunpowder to make the Powered version, which hits a little harder. Better metal hits harder and gets more of each hit through armour (for Spreadshot: more pellets that fly further), but you get fewer rounds per ingot. Ammunition Fired by From 1 Iron Ingot From 1 Steel Ingot From 1 Bronze Ingot From 1 Mythril Ingot Shot Rifles and pistols 64 Iron Shot 32 Steel Shot 16 Bronze Shot 8 Mythril Shot Spreadshot Shotguns 32 Iron Spreadshot 16 Steel Spreadshot 8 Bronze Spreadshot 4 Mythril Spreadshot Rocket Launchers 8 Iron Rocket 4 Steel Rocket 2 Bronze Rocket 1 Mythril Rocket Rifled barrels take Iron or Steel Shot and smoothbore barrels only Iron Shot. Bronze and Mythril Shot only fit a rifle with the Experimental Arclock. Spreadshot and Rockets of every metal fit any shotgun or launcher.

Craft the Gunsmithing Station on a crafting table and place it on the floor. Right-click it without sneaking. The Gun Assembly menu opens on a rifle. Click the button in the top-left corner to switch between rifle, pistol, shotgun and launcher. Each part slot already holds a part you are able to make. Click a slot to pick a different part. A barrier means you can't make any part for that slot yet. Pistols and launchers always show one in the stock slot, because they take no stock. Click the finished gun on the right. The materials for all its parts are taken from your inventory at once. Which parts you can use depends on your Smith perks from the Crafter profession, the same perks that unlock metals and woods for Advanced Crafting: Iron Smith for iron parts and oak stocks, Steel Smith for steel and maplewood, Abyssalite Smith for abyssalite and elderwood, and Mythril Smith for mythril and demonwood. Gun Parts Lowest perk Rifle Barrel, loader, chamber, action and stock. Iron Smith Pistol Barrel, loader, chamber and action. No stock. Iron Smith Shotgun Spread Barrel, loader, chamber, action and stock. Steel Smith Launcher Launcher Barrel, loader, chamber and Rocketlock. No stock. Abyssalite Smith The gun is named after its parts (a Matchlock Musket, a Steamlock Pistol, a Blunderbuss) and its look comes from its action, or from its barrel for shotguns and launchers. Its tooltip lists its stats and the ammunition it takes.

Hold the gun in your main hand with its ammunition in your inventory. When it is empty, right-click to reload. It loads as many rounds as it holds, or as many as you carry. Moving while you reload slows it down. Switching to another hotbar slot stops the reload and gives the ammo back. Right-click to fire. Revolvers and Quad Shot launchers fire several times before they need reloading. Sneak and right-click to choose which ammunition the next reload uses. If you run out of that kind, the reload fails until you choose another. Only one gun of each type stays loaded. Firing one unloads your other guns of the same type and gives their ammo back. Bullets drop over distance and fly through leaves and glass without breaking them. A shot to a player's head does extra damage. Shot and rockets push part of each hit straight through armour. Rockets explode when they hit something and hurt everyone nearby, you included, but they never break blocks. Your Charisma tightens your aim and speeds up your reloads.

A part's exact stats show in the Gun Assembly menu. Better metal and wood generally means a better gun. Part Fits Perk Cost Notes Smoothbore Barrel (Long) Rifle Iron Smith 4 Iron Ingot Fires Iron Shot. Rifled Barrel (Long) Rifle Steel Smith 4 Steel Ingot Fires Iron or Steel Shot, and aims better than smoothbore. Smoothbore Barrel (Short) Pistol Iron Smith 4 Iron Ingot Fires Iron Shot. Rifled Barrel (Short) Pistol Steel Smith 4 Steel Ingot Fires Iron or Steel Shot, and aims better than smoothbore. Spread Barrel Shotgun Steel Smith 4 Steel Ingot Fires Spreadshot of any metal. Makes the gun a shotgun. Launcher Barrel Launcher Abyssalite Smith 4 Abyssalite Ingot Fires Rockets of any metal. Makes the gun a launcher. Muzzle Loader All Iron Smith 2 Iron Ingot The basic loader. Breech Loader Rifle, Shotgun, Launcher Mythril Smith 2 Mythril Ingot Reloads much faster. Single Shot Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun Iron Smith 2 Iron Ingot Holds 1 shot. Single Shot (launcher) Launcher Abyssalite Smith 2 Abyssalite Ingot Holds 1 rocket. Shown in game as Single Shot. Quad Shot Launcher Mythril Smith 2 Mythril Ingot Holds 4 rockets. Revolver Rifle, Pistol Abyssalite Smith 2 Abyssalite Ingot Holds 6 shots, but reloads slowly and hits a little softer. Steamlock Rifle, Pistol Iron Smith 2 Iron Ingot Fires plain Iron Shot only, whatever the barrel. No smoke or muzzle flash, and a little less damage. Matchlock Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun Steel Smith 2 Steel Ingot The basic firing action. Flintlock Rifle, Pistol, Shotgun Abyssalite Smith 2 Abyssalite Ingot Aims and fires a little better than the Matchlock. Rocketlock Launcher Abyssalite Smith 2 Abyssalite Ingot The launcher's action. Experimental Arclock Rifle Mythril Smith 2 Mythril Ingot Fires only Bronze or Mythril Shot, whatever the barrel. Very accurate, but slow to fire and reload. Oak Stock Rifle, Shotgun Iron Smith 2 Refined Barkwood Steadies your aim. Maplewood Stock Rifle, Shotgun Steel Smith 2 Refined Maplewood Steadies your aim more. Elderwood Stock Rifle, Shotgun Abyssalite Smith 2 Refined Elderwood Steadies your aim even more. Demonwood Stock Rifle, Shotgun Mythril Smith 2 Refined Demonwood Steadies your aim the most.
Some provinces are overrun by monsters. Walk into one and they keep coming at you, day and night. Fight a wave at a Lure and win, and the province is cleared. Updated 23 Oct 2026
Command What it does /lure leave Gives up the Lure fight you joined, so leaving the province no longer hurts you.

sectionTitle: Clearing a province with a Lure
text: Make a Lure at the Block Station from 2 Oak Planks. You need to be playing a character to place or join one. Place the Lure on the ground inside an infested province. You join its fight automatically. It does nothing in a province that isn't infested, and each province can only have one Lure at a time. Everyone in the province gets 20 seconds to decide: right-click the Lure to join, or leave the province. Then the wave starts: 20, 40, 60 or 80 monsters from Mild to Extreme, let out over about two minutes. Monsters already roaming the province join the wave, and the normal spawning stops until the fight ends. The label above the Lure counts how many are left. Right-click the Lure during the fight to make the remaining monsters glow for 10 seconds. There is no time limit. Kill the last monster and the province is cleared. If everyone who joined dies or gives up, the infestation stays. Warning Once a fight starts, nobody can stand by and watch: If you are in the province and haven't joined, you lose a heart every second. You can still join by right-clicking the Lure. If you joined and then leave the province, you lose a heart every second until you come back or give up with /lure leave. If you joined and log out, you have 5 minutes to come back. After that, that character dies the next time you play it, unless the fight has already ended. The Lure can't be broken while it is in use, and it disappears when the fight ends, win or lose. A fight still running at the daily restart is lost, with no penalty for anyone.

While you are in an infested province, monsters keep spawning around you, a little way off rather than right next to you. The worse the infestation, the more of them and the faster they come. They don't spawn below Y 56. You get ghouls, rats, slime cubes and skeletons, and bug-like creatures that burst into parasitic worms when they die. The worms bite through armour and poison you.

Every infestation is in bog provinces, mostly in and around the Westmarshes, overrun by Bog Monsters. On the website map, pick the Infestation map mode: each infested province is coloured by how bad it is, from yellow to dark red, and hovering over it names the level. There are four levels: Mild, Worrying, Severe and Extreme. Left alone, an infestation slowly gets worse and can spread into neighbouring bog provinces, even ones that were cleared before.

Lock your doors with a key and choose who can open your chests. You need to be playing a character for any of it. Updated 23 Oct 2026
Command What it does /thievery clearclues Then right-click one of your doors or containers within 30 seconds to wipe the clues left at it.

Any chest, barrel or other container you place is yours, and so are armour stands, item frames, artifact displays and pedestals. They start out Public. Sneak and left-click one to change who can use it. Each click moves to the next setting: Setting Who can use it Private Only you. Guild You and everyone in your guild. Faction Every guild in your faction. Public Anyone. Guild and faction mean your guild and its faction. Your other characters count as strangers. Nobody can break a container they can't open, or turn your chest into a double chest with theirs. Hoppers only move items between containers that have the same owner. Ender chests are not part of this: everyone sees only their own.

Pick up the first item in your inventory and click it onto the second. No station is needed. You can make one paper copy of the same key every 4 hours. Pick up Click onto You get Clay Ball Iron Key or Golden Key Key Mold. The clay is used up. Copper Ingot Key Mold Copper Key. It works like the original. The mold is used up. Paper Iron Key, Golden Key or Copper Key Paper Key. It opens the door once and then falls apart. It can't lock or unlock.

Make an Iron Key at the Tool Station from 2 Iron Ingots. A goldsmith can make a Golden Key, which is harder to pick. Hold the key, sneak and right-click a door, trapdoor or fence gate to lock it. Do it again to unlock. Iron doors and iron trapdoors are the only ones that can't be locked. A locked door only opens for its key or a copy, though anyone can close a locked door or gate. Only someone holding the original key, a Copper Key copy, or a key chain with either can break it, or the block under it. A Key Chain (Tool Station, 2 Iron Ingots) holds up to 5 keys and opens their doors, but it can't lock or unlock. Click a key onto it to add it, and right-click the chain in your inventory to take the last key off.

A lock stops most people, but someone with a lockpick can still get in: Your locks can only be picked while you, or someone from the guild the lock belongs to, is online, and for a short while after. A Faction lock lets your whole faction in, but a thief who picks one can carry off much more than from a Private or Guild lock. Thieves often leave clues behind. You can wipe the clues at your own door or container with the command below, though you may want to read them first.

Mages cast spells from runes set into a staff, wand or blade. You build the weapon at a Magic Station, attune it to an element with aura gathered at a shrine, and raise your own Resonance by meditating. A spell only casts if your Resonance in its element is high enough. Updated 20 Oct 2026

Three weapon shapes, each wanting a different set of parts. Archetype In-game name Melee Parts it needs Staff Mage Staff No Core, Handle, Tome x3 Wand Wand No Core, Handle, Tome Sword Mage Blade Yes Core, Handle, Tome

Choose a cast mode in /resonance. Flow is the default. Every spell you cast moves your Equilibrium. In Surge it moves toward Corruption, and in Flow toward Tranquility. Meditation moves it too, but there the orb you hit decides the direction, not your cast mode (see Meditation). Both sides make your spells cheaper, stronger or quicker to recharge, and the effect grows the further you go. Corruption gives its bonus early. Once you have any, it keeps growing on its own, faster the deeper you are, and its bonus gets weaker again near the extreme. Tranquility needs to build up before it helps much, but its bonus ends up stronger. It slowly fades back toward neutral if you stop.

Hold the weapon and use the rune's casting key. The default is right-click. To change a rune's casting key, hold the rune and use /magic rune keybind. What you see Why What it costs you *Whiff* The weapon's Rift made the cast fail, or you are carrying more than one staff ("Too many staffs"). Mana and the cooldown, both already spent. *Refused* Your Resonance is below what the weapon asks, or the weapon holds no element at all. Nothing. *Damaged* The weapon holds runes that no longer fit. Nothing, but the weapon will not cast until you reclaim its runes. A refusal tells you why in chat, for example "This spell needs Cerrith II. You carry I.", but at most once every 30 seconds for each weapon and element. To fix a Damaged weapon, right-click an empty Magic Station with it. The station removes the loose runes and gives them back.

A single-use item that carries aura from a shrine to your weapon. Charges are crafted at the Rune Station from Enchanted Dust: 4, 8, 12 and 16 dust for tiers I to IV. Enchanted Charge I Rune Station Crafting time: 10 seconds Enchanted Dust 4 → Enchanted Charge I Enchanted Charge II Rune Station Crafting time: 10 seconds Enchanted Dust 8 → Enchanted Charge II Enchanted Charge III Rune Station Crafting time: 10 seconds Enchanted Dust 12 → Enchanted Charge III Enchanted Charge IV Rune Station Crafting time: 10 seconds Enchanted Dust 16 → Enchanted Charge IV The band printed on a charge, such as "Cerrith II", shows how much aura of that element it holds: under 10 shows a dash, 10 is I, 35 is II, 65 is III and 95 is IV. Spells use the same bands for Resonance, so a spell that needs Cerrith II needs at least 35 Cerrith Resonance.

View your Resonance profile and change a rune's casting key. Command Aliases What it does /magic rune keybind None While holding a rune, use this command to change its casting key. /resonance /res Opens your Resonance profile: a bar per element, your Equilibrium (Corruption vs Tranquility), your Mental Points, and the Surge / Flow cast-mode toggle.

Be a Mage. Only Mages can use Mage Staffs, Mage Wands, Mage Blades and Mage Armor. Mage gear is expensive, so plan for the cost. Build a weapon. Craft and place a Magic Station, right-click it to open the assembly menu, and put the parts together. See Archetypes for the parts each weapon needs. Fill a charge. Craft an Enchanted Charge at the Rune Station and place it on a pedestal in a shrine. Attune the weapon. Hold the filled charge and right-click the weapon on its Magic Station. This starts the orb minigame, which decides how much of the charge the weapon keeps. The station keeps a new weapon until it has been attuned. Take the weapon. Right-click the station with an empty hand. Charge it again later. Hold the weapon and right-click an empty Magic Station to set it down, then attune it with another charge. A later charge can only raise the weapon's attunement, never lower it. Start over. To clear a weapon's attunement instead, sneak and right-click an empty Magic Station while holding it. Chat shows the fee, half the materials of the weapon's parts, rounded up. Sneak and right-click again to pay it. The next charge that stores anything replaces the old attunement and its Rift. Until then, only you can charge the weapon or take it back. When no charge is running, sneak and left-click the station to get the weapon and the fee. Add runes. Put spell runes into the weapon's sockets. Every spell comes from a rune, so a weapon with no runes casts nothing. Raise your Resonance by meditating. A new character starts with none, and even the weakest spells need some. Cast. Hold the weapon and use the rune's casting key. The default is right-click.

Meditating in a ring of artifacts is how you raise your own Resonance. Place 8 pedestals in a ring, all on the same level as the centre block: one 4 blocks north, south, east and west of the centre, and one on each diagonal, 3 blocks across and 3 blocks along. Put artifacts on the pedestals. You gain Resonance in the elements those artifacts hold. The ring does not need to be a shrine. Sit down on the centre block, for example with /sit. Meditation starts by itself. A white orb appears where you are looking. Hit it (look at it and left-click) to begin. More orbs then circle you. Each hit costs 1 Mental Point and raises your Resonance. Blue orbs move your Equilibrium toward Tranquility, and red orbs toward Corruption. Hitting a red orb turns the orbs red for a few seconds. Stand up to stop. "Meditation complete at this site" means this ring has nothing more to give you for now. Resonance per orb hit Up to 4 Mental Point cost per hit 1 Mental Point pool 150shared with Research Regeneration +10 / houroffline too Mental Points (also called Focus) are shared between meditation and Research experiments. Each point of Wisdom adds 0.5 to your hourly regeneration, and each point of Intelligence adds 0.25. An empty pool takes 15 hours to refill at the base rate. Resonance fades, and stored artifacts get muffled Your Resonance drops by 0.02 every real hour, so it slowly falls if you stop meditating. If several people meditate with the same artifact, what it gives is split between them. An artifact holding aura becomes muffled if you keep it in a chest or other container, with no message. A muffled artifact gives less when you meditate, and it is fully muffled after 24 hours. Keep artifacts in your inventory, on a pedestal, on an artifact display or in an item frame. There they recover fully over 7 days.

Attuning a weapon starts a timed minigame. The charge is used up as soon as it starts. Hold the charge and right-click the weapon on its Magic Station. Orbs then circle the station. Look at an orb and left-click to hit it. Pale blue orbs are good. Each one you hit stores more of the charge in the weapon. Hit enough before time runs out and the weapon keeps the whole charge. Each pale blue orb that fades before you hit it costs you 8% of the charge. Rust-orange orbs are bad. Each one you hit adds 5 Rift to the weapon, up to 100. Higher-tier charges have faster orbs and fewer good ones. If you disconnect, the run ends and the weapon keeps what you had stored so far. Using a charge above your Resonance If a charge needs more Resonance than you have, a warning lists what you are missing. Right-click again to use it anyway. That second click spends the charge. Rift per bad orb +5capped at 100 Rift removed per later recharge 10never on the first charge Rift stays on the weapon A failed cast still uses its mana and starts its cooldown. Each later successful charge on the weapon removes 10 Rift. The first charge never removes any.

A socket takes a rune of its own tier or any tier below it. It never takes a bigger one. Craft quality of the gear Socket it gets Rune that fits Rusted None Nothing Tempered Minor Minor Polished Lesser Minor, Lesser Gleaming Greater Minor, Lesser, Greater Masterwork Ascendant Any tier The socket comes from how well the piece was crafted, not from its material. Iron Mage armour can take an Ascendant Armor Rune, but only if that piece came out Masterwork. A Tempered iron piece has a Minor socket, so a Minor Armor Rune is the most it will ever hold. Armor runes go on Mage armour only. Every other armour piece has a Gemstone socket instead, and an armor rune will not fit it. Armor runes and weapon runes are separate: an armor rune never fits a staff, wand or blade, and a spell rune never fits armour. A smaller rune in a bigger socket works, but it uses that socket up. If a piece has several sockets, the rune goes into the smallest one that can hold it. Check the socket line in the item's lore before you spend the dust. It names the biggest size the piece accepts. Quality is decided while smithing, see Advanced Crafting.

A shrine fills artifacts and charges with aura. A shrine is a Pedestal and everything within 4 blocks of it in every direction, above and below included. Build that space with blocks that suit an element, and use a mix of different matching blocks rather than one kind. A shrine scores each element separately, so one shrine can serve more than one. Put an artifact or a charge on the pedestal and it starts filling with aura. A blank charge first takes on every element the shrine gives. A weak shrine cannot fill a high-tier charge. A pedestal that is part of a meditation ring does not fill anything.

A plain vanilla 3x3 craft. Anyone can make one. Magic Station Crafting Table Requires: None Blackstone Blackstone Blackstone Blackstone Gold Ingot Blackstone Blackstone Amethyst Shard Blackstone → Magic Station Place it, then interact to open the weapon assembly menu.

Terms used on the rest of this page. Term What it means Element A school of magic: Cerrith, Oseni, Seithr or Mitlan. Each element has its own runes, shrines and Resonance. Resonance Your character's skill in one element, from 0 to 100. Each spell needs a minimum Resonance in its element. Higher Resonance also lowers mana cost and cooldowns and raises damage. Aura Magical energy stored in artifacts and charges. A shrine fills them with aura, and you spend a charge's aura to attune a weapon. Aura stored in an artifact never fades. Artifact A magical object that holds aura. On a pedestal in a shrine it fills with aura. In a meditation ring it lets you meditate. Shrine A pedestal and the blocks around it. The blocks you build around the pedestal decide which elements the shrine gives. Enchanted Charge A single-use item. You fill it at a shrine, then spend it to attune a weapon. Socket A slot in a finished weapon that holds one spell rune. Sockets come in four sizes: Minor, Lesser, Greater and Ascendant. A socket takes a rune of its own size or smaller. Attunement Locking an element into a weapon by spending a charge on it. A weapon with no element will not cast. Equilibrium Your balance between Corruption and Tranquility, shown in /resonance. Your cast mode decides which way it moves. Rift The chance, in percent, that a cast fails. A weapon gains Rift when you hit the wrong orbs while attuning it. Magic progress belongs to your character Resonance and Equilibrium are stored on your active character, so a second character starts from zero. /resonance does not open without an active character.

A Market Block is a shop you place yourself: right-click it and sell raw materials for denars. It only buys, so you cannot purchase items back from it. The more of one material the block has already absorbed, the less it pays for the next bundle, and that price slowly recovers if you leave it alone. Updated 27 Sept 2026

Craft a Market Block (recipe below) and place it. Right-click it to open Market Categories: Metal, Mineral, Stone, Wood, Farm, Fish, Alchemy. Click a category to see its trades, each showing the item, its current price, and a demand bar. Click a trade to sell a full bundle of that item for denars, paid straight into your pouch. Market Block Crafting Table Requires: None Ink Sac Paper Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks → Synthetic Ink can replace the Ink Sac. Use one Oak Plank in each of the five plank slots.

Instruments turn your hotbar into a keyboard. Hold one in your off-hand and press 1 through 8. Hold Shift for a second layer of chords or higher notes. There are nine instruments, each with a completely different sound. Other players hear you from about 64 blocks away. All nine are crafted at the Instrument Station and crafting them requires the Bard class, but anyone can play one, so an instrument you are given or buy works fine. Updated 13 Oct 2026 Flute Lute Vielle Trumpet Celtic Harp Kalimba Dulcimer Accordion Bagpipe

Command Aliases What it does Notes /instruments keybinds None Prints the full note and chord layout for the instrument currently in your off-hand. You must be holding an instrument in your off-hand, or it just tells you so. Permission instruments.use, default true - no normal player is ever blocked. /instruments list None Prints the name of every instrument that exists on the server. Needs nothing in hand. Permission instruments.use, default true - no normal player is ever blocked.

"My instrument makes no sound." Three things, in order. One: your Jukebox/Note Blocks volume slider must not be at zero: notes play in the Records category, not Master or Ambient. Two: the instrument must be in your off-hand. Three: press 1–8; slot 9 is the reset slot and plays nothing. "Can I craft an instrument without being a Bard?" No: all nine recipes require the Bard class. "Can I play an instrument without being a Bard?" Yes. Anyone can play one.

Put the instrument in your off-hand. Your main hand is irrelevant. Press number keys 1 to 8 to play notes. The scale runs: 1=C, 2=D, 3=E, 4=F, 5=G, 6=A, 7=B, 8=C (an octave up). Hold Shift and press 1 to 8 for the second layer. On most instruments that's a full chord; on the Flute, Trumpet and Bagpipe it's the same scale an octave higher, giving sixteen notes total. After every note your selection snaps back to slot 9, so you can hit the same note twice in a row. Whatever sits in slot 9 is what bystanders see in your main hand while you play. A single note particle appears above your head with each note, so everyone can tell it is you.

The Recycling Station breaks crafted gear back down into some of the materials that made it. Updated 22 Oct 2026
Made on a crafting table and placed on the floor. Recycling Station Crafting Table Requires: None Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks → Recycling Station

Right-click the station to open it. Click the item in your inventory to move it in. Click it again in the station to take it back. Items that can't be recycled, or that are unbreakable, are refused. The right side of the menu shows what you would get back. Click the confirm button in the top-left corner. The materials pop out of the station, and anyone nearby can grab them. Gear returns at most half of what went into it, less the more worn it is. Each material is rounded down, so a material that went in only once won't come back, and fully broken gear gives nothing. If nothing would come back, confirming tells you so and you keep the item. If you close the menu with an item still in it, you get the item back. With a full inventory, it waits for your character until you have room.

Item Returns Forged weapons and armour Up to half the materials. An alloy comes back as its base metal or wood and its crystals. Guns Up to half the materials the gun was made from. Broken guns and guns made before tracking began can't. Mage weapons Up to half the materials paid to craft it. Take any runes out first. Broken ones can't. Gold jewellery Up to half the gold. The gem is not returned. Spell runes 2, 4, 6 or 8 Enchanted Dust (Minor to Ascendant). Armour runes 4, 8, 12 or 16 Enchanted Dust (Minor to Ascendant). Artifacts Enchanted Dust by rarity: 4, 8, 12, 16 or 28 (Common to Legendary). Any stored aura is lost. Spent husks Half an artifact's dust: 2, 4, 6, 8 or 14. Unusable Scrap Each material in it has a chance to come back; its tooltip shows the odds. The scrap is used up either way. Vanilla items can't be recycled.
Research is an item-based deduction puzzle. Make a research paper at a Cartography Table, study it at a Lectern, and test materials to uncover and fill its hidden aspects. Updated 27 Sept 2026

Rule Meaning Primary / secondary aspect An item contributes more strongly to each primary aspect than to each secondary aspect. One item can contribute to several aspects. Rejected An aspect outside the hidden recipe is rejected after enough testing. An experiment containing only rejected aspects is blocked. Undiscovered Aspect Its row appears after you make some progress toward the required points. Intelligence makes it appear sooner. Confirmed Its identity appears after further progress. Intelligence makes it appear sooner. Confirmation is not completion: keep filling it. Product reveal The product appears after enough aspects are confirmed. Intelligence can make it appear sooner, but early reveal is not assured. Completion Every hidden aspect must reach its full required points. Total points are not an experiment count, because tests may contribute to multiple aspects. A concrete experiment example Arcane Crystal is a primary Arcane item, so it supplies 2 Arcane points when tested. Crying Obsidian is secondary Arcane and supplies 1. These are distinct items, so each can be tested once. The Arcane Crystal project requires 3 Arcane points, plus its Earth, Energy and Machine requirements.

Maximum Focus 150Stored per RP character; shared with Magic meditation Each experiment 1 point Base refill 10 per real hourRegenerates offline; 15 hours from empty to full Wisdom adds 0.5 points per hour per attribute point; Intelligence adds 0.25. The regeneration interval is one hour. When exhausted, the lectern tells you that you are too tired to research. The aspect table counts distinct primary and secondary items; it is not a recipe or a list of required quantities.

sectionTitle: Make a paper and start a project
text: Sneak-right-click a Cartography Table to open the Research Station. Combine one vanilla Paper and one Alchemy Powder for one Parchment Paper. It takes 2 seconds. Combine one Parchment Paper with the subject ingredient. Every paper, including an Unknown Research Paper, takes 5 seconds. Every station recipe grants 10 Herborist EXP. Recipes hide when you lack their ingredients. Hold the resulting paper and right-click a Lectern. Each lectern has one owner, so find another lectern if one is occupied. A Minor, Lesser, Greater or Ascendant Runestone (weapon or armour) can start its own project without first becoming a paper. Choose an experiment item, inspect its point preview, then confirm. Each different item may be tested once per project. Items with no aspect tags cannot be used. Use the Testing, Confirmed and Rejected labels to guide your next experiment. Fill every required aspect completely, then collect the result that drops above the lectern. It is not placed directly in your inventory. Warning Breaking the lectern destroys the project. The Scrap button also destroys it after a confirmation and does not refund the project.
Small tools for setting a scene: sit down, lie down or crawl, pose armor stands, put on a mask, and give your items their own names and lore. Every player can use them. Updated 22 Oct 2026

/tfmc statues gives you the Armor Statues book, free and as often as you need it. Open the book and click an option to change the nearest armor stand within 3 blocks. Use Check Target first: it makes the stand that will be edited glow for a few seconds. Category What you can change Settings Arms, base plate, size, visibility, gravity and visual fire Poses Ready-made poses such as Salute, Facepalm and Stargazing, a random pose, or each limb by hand Position Rotation, small moves, aligning the stand to a block, and scale from 0.25 to 3 times Tools Mirror and flip, copy and paste a pose, swap equipment slots, and undo or redo Locking a stand stops accidental edits and equipment clicks, but it does not protect the stand from other players.

Command Aliases What it does Notes /sit None Sits you down where you stand. None /sit toggle None Turns sitting by right-clicking stairs, slabs, carpets and snow on or off. On by default. /lay /glay Lie down. None /layback /glayback Lie on your back. None /bellyflop /gbellyflop Lie face down. None /spin /gspin Spin around on the ground. None /crawl /gcrawl Drop down and crawl. Double-tapping sneak does not start a crawl here. /tfmc statues None Gives you the Armor Statues book. None /tfmc masks None Gives you a random mask. Once every 10 seconds. /tfmc patterns None Gives you all ten banner patterns. Once every 10 seconds.

Craft them at the Tool Station. Pick the stone up on your cursor and click it onto a single, unstacked item in your inventory, then type your text in chat within 60 seconds, or type cancel. A Lorestone adds a line of lore, and typing clear instead removes all of the item's lore. A Namestone renames the item. If something goes wrong, you get the stone back. A line can be up to 100 characters, colour codes included, and an item can have up to 10 lore lines, counting the ones it already has. Use & colour codes or &#RRGGBB hex colours. If you type a name without colour codes, the namestone offers a palette you can click, or you can type a colour name or a hex value. Lorestone Tool Station Crafting time: 5 seconds Gold Ingot → Lorestone Namestone Tool Station Crafting time: 5 seconds Iron Ingot → Namestone

/tfmc masks gives you a random mask. Most masks hide who you are while you wear them on your head: in-character chat shows you as Masked, and nobody can read your character card. /tfmc patterns gives you all ten banner patterns for the loom: Flower, Guster, Field Masoned, Skull, Thing, Globe, Snout, Flow, Creeper and Bordure Indented. You can use each command once every 10 seconds.

/lay, /layback, /bellyflop and /spin put you in a pose, and /crawl drops you to a crawl. Sneak to get back up. While posed you cannot use blocks, items or other players, so save poses for a quiet moment. Lying down counts towards skipping the night when someone else is in a bed.

Right-click a stair, slab, carpet or snow layer with an empty hand, from up to 3 blocks away, to sit on it. You sit where you clicked, and on stairs you face the way the stair faces. Only the bottom half of stairs and slabs works. You can also type /sit to sit where you stand. Several players can share a block, but you cannot sit on other players. Sneak to stand up. Taking damage does not unseat you, but breaking the block under you does. If you keep sitting down by accident while building, /sit toggle turns click-to-sit off; /sit still works.
Your Minecraft account, your Discord account and the TFMC website work together once they are linked. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Command What it does Notes /linkdiscord Gives you a code to link your Discord account. Run /linkdiscord <code> in the Discord server. You cannot play in Survival until you are linked. /unlinkdiscord Removes your Discord link. You will need to link again to play in Survival. /token create profile Gives you a one-time code to sign in to your profile on the website. None /token create <skin|drink> Gives you a one-time code to upload a custom skin or drink on the website. Noble rank and above. Skin and drink codes share one cooldown. /patreon [unlink] Links your Patreon account, shows your supporter status, or removes the link. None /tfmc patreon Shows the link to the server's Patreon page. None /tfmc tips <enable|disable> Turns the tips shown in chat on or off. None /tfmc pack [auto|manual] Loads the server resource pack now, or sets whether it loads automatically when you join. None /tfmc map Gives you the link to the nations map on the website. None /tfmc date Shows today's weekday and month in the world's own calendar. None /tcore stats <advancedcrafting|factions|rpcharacters|skills|vehicles> Shows your own statistics for that part of the game. None /tfmc drinks Opens the drink builder. Noble rank and above. /tfmc booster Starts a one-hour profession EXP booster for everyone on the server. Ascended and Legacy only, once every 3 days.

Supporter ranks come from Patreon. Run /patreon to link your Patreon account and see your status, and /patreon unlink to remove the link. The Noble, Gilded and Ascended ranks follow your Patreon tier. /tfmc patreon shows the Patreon page.

Run /token create profile in game for a one-time code, then enter it on your profile to sign in. There you can create characters, change their wills, manage wardrobes and kits, and see your custom skins and drinks and your linked accounts.

/token create skin and /token create drink give you a code for uploading a custom skin or drink on the website. They are a supporter perk, and both share one cooldown that depends on your rank. Rank Skin or drink code Commoner Not available Noble Every 28 days Gilded Every 21 days Ascended Every 14 days Legacy Every 7 days

You cannot play in Survival until your Discord account is linked; until then you are held in place. Type /linkdiscord in game to get a code you can click to copy, then run /linkdiscord <code> in the TFMC Discord server. The game confirms the link within a second or so. /unlinkdiscord removes it again. If you leave the Discord server, you have a grace period to rejoin. After that your account is unlinked and you cannot play in Survival until you link again.

Thieves pick locks and pockets, and bandits rob people and loot the graves of those they kill. To protect your own things, see Locks & Keys. Updated 23 Oct 2026

Thief and Bandit are evil archetypes. Once your account is a day old, you can give one or both to a character whose personality fits when you create it. A Thief can pick chests and display furniture and pick pockets. Anyone with a lockpick can pick a door. A Bandit can rob players and loot graves. Warning Lockpicking, pickpocketing, robbing and grave looting each start a 30-minute evil RP session, and doing any of them again starts it over. During a session, any strike you take in a started PvP fight kills your character outright (see death and graves).

Picking a door or display can leave a clue behind, and taking from a chest always does. A clue is one of the clues you wrote for your character or a hint at your race, and once in a while it names you outright. Other characters nearby slowly notice clues until they fade away. Pickpocketing and robbery leave no clues at the scene.

Command What it does /thievery loadout Choose which kinds of items you can see and take. Thief only. /pickpocket start Then right-click a player within 4 blocks to pick their pocket. Thief only. /robbery start Then right-click a player within 4 blocks to demand a robbery. Bandit only. /robbery accept Accepts a robbery demanded of you. Anyone can use it.

Right-click a locked container as a Thief. You are held in place while you work. A ring of tumblers appears. Press the movement key shown in the middle while the pointer is in the green zone. Set all 4 to open the lock. One slip and it fails. Sneak to give up. The container opens hidden. Click a slot to look at it: the first look is always safe, and each safe slot shows how many seized pins are next to it. Right-click a slot to mark it as a pin. Clicking a pin snaps a lockpick and ends the search, but you can still take what you found. Take the items you uncovered that your loadout lets you see. You or your guild can only pick the same container once every 3 days.

Locked artifact displays, pedestals, armour stands and item frames can be picked as a Thief with a Strong Lockpick, from within 3 blocks, using the same bar as doors. On a success, whatever your loadout lets you see goes straight into your inventory.

Right-click a locked door within 3 blocks. A bar runs across your screen: right-click again when the marker is on green. Red breaks your lockpick, yellow just fails, and walking away cancels. A picked door swings open and stays unlocked for everyone for an hour. A door locked with a Golden Key needs a Strong Lockpick.
A Bandit who kills a player can rob their locked grave without a lockpick. One right-click takes everything your loadout lets you see, as far as your inventory has room.

Before stealing, a Thief picks which kinds of items they know how to spot with /thievery loadout. Each kind costs points, and you have 10 at most. Adding a kind uses points that come back at 1 an hour; removing one gives nothing back. Your loadout is shared by all the characters on your account. When you steal, items of kinds you didn't pick show as HIDDEN! and can't be taken. You can only carry off so much each time, so pricey items may not fit at all.

The Basic Lockpick (1 Steel Ingot) and the stronger Strong Lockpick (2 Steel Ingots) are made at the Tool Station. Hold one and right-click what you want to open. When a lockpick breaks, only one from the stack is lost. After a failed try, give it a minute before trying the same lock again.

Run /pickpocket start and right-click someone within 4 blocks. You are held in place. Press jump quickly to fill the ring twice within 30 seconds. Their main inventory opens (not their hotbar or armour). Take what you can, and stay within 4 blocks or it ends. Each pocket you look through may let your mark hear something rummaging in their bag. A botched attempt always gets noticed, and sometimes they see exactly who it was. You or your guild can only pickpocket the same person once an hour.

A robbery is a hold-up both players agree to play out. As a Bandit, run /robbery start and right-click someone within 4 blocks. They have 30 seconds to accept with /robbery accept or the button in chat. Once they accept, they are frozen and can't be hurt or touch their inventory. You get 2 minutes to look through everything they carry, armour included. If your loadout includes money, their coin pouch is there too: click it to take 10 denars, or shift-click for 100. Closing the menu ends the robbery. If your victim logs out during it, everything they carry drops. You or your guild can only rob the same person once every 3 days.

Open /professions and buy Engineer ranks in the Crafter profession. Engineer I costs 1 point for ground vehicles. Engineer II requires I and costs 2 more points for ships. Engineer III requires II and costs 3 more points for aircraft. Craft and place an Engineering Table for land vehicles, fixed guns and aircraft, or a Dockyard for ships. Use the crafting-table patterns below. Right-click the station, choose a category and select a blueprint that your Engineer rank unlocks. Gather its listed materials before selecting the building spot. Left-click the intended spawn point within 12 blocks of the station. Choose it within 30 seconds of selecting the blueprint. The materials are consumed when you choose the spot. Wait for the build to finish. Stay within 96 blocks so the completed vehicle can appear, then right-click it to claim it and select a seat. Engineering Table Crafting Table Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks → Engineering Table Dockyard Crafting Table Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Iron Ingot Oak Planks Iron Ingot Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks Oak Planks → Dockyard A cargo cart to start with The Wooden Cart needs Engineer I, 64 Oak Logs, 16 Iron Ingots and 16 Sticks. It takes two hours to build and carries 54 cargo slots. Warning Breaking the construction station during a build cancels construction and drops the materials at the station. Collect them before they despawn.

Enter: right-click the vehicle and choose a seat. Shift reopens seat selection while aboard. Only the captain steers. Drive: run /vf keybinds while seated to see the controls for your vehicle. W/S commonly adjusts throttle and A/D steers. Controls can change between ground, flight and water. Refuel: hold the fuel listed on the vehicle page and right-click once per item. Each Coal Block or Arcane Fuel adds 100 fuel units. Stop an Arcane Fuel engine before refuelling; Coal Blocks can be added while an engine runs. Carry cargo: right-click a vehicle with storage to open its containers. Wooden Cart and Cloudskimmer each hold 54 slots. Behemoth has four 54-slot holds. Coal Car holds 27 slots of Coal Blocks. Tow: sneak-right-click a Wooden Cart or Field Artillery, then sneak-right-click a Horse Cart to connect it. Repeat on the towing vehicle to detach. Stay within eight blocks while making the connection. Save fuel by stopping the engine Fuel burns at the same rate at any throttle above or below zero; zero throttle uses none. Locomotive overdrive above 100% burns more. A damaged engine also limits maximum throttle, so repair it to restore power.

Claim a new vehicle by right-clicking it. A claimed vehicle starts with an owner-only whitelist. Open Ownership Settings in Select Seat to allow other players, add a player by name or enable passenger tickets. With tickets enabled, hold Paper and right-click your vehicle to make matching tickets for passengers. Reset Owner releases ownership. Clicking an occupied yellow seat ejects its passenger and prevents re-entry for 60 seconds. Use /vf findvehicles to locate your vehicles. Vehicles more than 160 blocks from players unload into storage; they are not destroyed.

Hold Vehicle Repair and right-click a grounded, stationary vehicle, or use a mechanic seat to repair while aboard. Use the Repair Tool in the menu to fix components and the Water Bucket for fires. Keep the menu open and stay nearby until repair finishes. Hold Vehicle Paint and right-click to open Select Skin. Engineer Station tool Materials Time Requirement Vehicle Repair 4 Iron Ingots 5 seconds Vehicle Mechanic profession Vehicle Paint 1 Common Item Skin Scroll 5 seconds Vehicle Mechanic and Gilded rank or higher Vehicle Mechanic costs two Crafter profession points. Keep ship pumps repaired to control flooding. Repair damaged engines and wings to recover performance.
Choose a vehicle above, then select one of its available skins beside the preview. In game, use Vehicle Paint to choose from the skins available to you.

Build trains on custom train tracks. Craft Train Track in batches of 64 at the Block Station. Leave room for wide bends and gentle slopes: turns have a 35-degree limit, and slopes have a 10-degree maximum. Track item Use Track Small lay a short segment Track Medium lay a medium segment Track Large lay a long segment Train Track the track piece itself (64 per craft at the Block Station) Railroad Switch switch/junction marker

Choose the seat assigned to a weapon. Hold its ammunition and right-click to reload, then use Space to fire. W/S adjusts elevation and A/D traverses; mounted rifles aim toward your cursor. Check /vf keybinds for the controls of your current seat. Weapon Reload Ammunition Mounted Rifle 5 s Bullet Box Naval Cannon 5 s Cannonball (+ Clusterbomb on some) Anti-Air Turret 10 s Bullet Box Autocannon 5 s Flak Shells Flak Cannon 10 s Flak Shells Ammunition Rounds per item Bullet Box 100 Flak Shells 30 Cannonball 1 Small Bomb 1 Small Bomb (rack) 8 Clusterbomb 1 Torpedo 1 Note Each barrel receives a load of ammunition. One Bullet Box loads 200 rounds into the Biplane's two-barrel Front Rifles. Small Bomb Racks supply eight bombs per load. Mounted weapons use vehicle ammunition from the Engineer Station. Right-click an idle Woodworking Station, choose a style, then a piece. Right-click the station with materials to add them one at a time. The title shows how many of each material type the piece still needs, but not which ones. Once all the materials are in, left-click the station with the tools. The title counts tools by group (see the table below), so full counts don't mean you used the right tools. Left-click with the Branding Tool to finish. The piece appears on top of the station. Right-click with it to see your progress, or sneak and left-click to cancel and get your materials back. Finishing shows your Recipe, Hits and Total percentages. Only exact work makes the piece: the right materials, and the right number of hits with each tool. If either is off, it is ruined and the materials are lost. If someone breaks the station mid-project, the materials go to whoever broke it.

Valewood, Runebark, Amberpine, Goldmaple, Silk. With the Herborist perk Tree Gatherer III, chopping any log or wood block can drop them. A Forestry node set to Rare Wood produces them too, once it has Diamond Axes or better. Spare wood sells at a Market Block.
